title: The separability retraction on sheaf tensor products
statement: Let $F\to B$ be a field extension and let $J$ be a site with sheafification. Let $\underline F,\underline B$ be the constant ring sheaves and let $U:\operatorname{Mod}(\underline B)\to\operatorname{Mod}(\underline F)$ be restriction of scalars. Suppose $e\in B\otimes_F B$ satisfies $\mu(e)=1$ and $(b\otimes1-1\otimes b)e=0$ for every $b\in B$. The bifunctor $T(M,N)=UM\otimes_{\underline F}UN$ admits a natural ring action $a:B\otimes_F B\to\operatorname{End}(T)$, a natural quotient $q:T\to U(M\otimes_{\underline B}N)$ and a natural section $s$ with $s;q=1$ and $q;s=a(e)$. On pure sheaf tensor sections, $a(b\otimes c)$ sends $m\otimes n$ to $bm\otimes cn$, and $q$ sends $m\otimes_F n$ to $m\otimes_B n$. The statement concerns module sheaves only, without complexes, derived categories, finiteness or resolutions.

proof.text: The commuting coefficient actions define the tensor-algebra action on sheaf tensor products. Sheafify the canonical balanced quotient, preserving its pure-section formula.

Write e as a finite sum a_i tensor b_i. Define the section on a balanced generator m tensor_B n by sum_i a_i m tensor_F b_i n. The annihilator identities give B-balancing. Extend through constant-presheaf module sheafification; uniqueness handles locally constant sections and proves naturality.

Evaluate the two composites on pure tensors. The balanced quotient of the e-action is multiplication by mu(e)=1, whereas section after quotient is the e-action itself. Tensor induction, followed by uniqueness of bilinear sheafification extension, proves both identities on all sections. The same uniqueness proves naturality in each module; all constructions also apply to zero modules and the empty site.

theorem exists_separableFieldTensorSheaf (e : B ⊗[F] B)
    (hμ : Algebra.TensorProduct.lmul' F e = 1)
    (he : ∀ b : B, (b ⊗ₜ[F] (1 : B) - (1 : B) ⊗ₜ[F] b) * e = 0) :
    ∃ (a : (B ⊗[F] B) →+* End (sheafSource J F B))
      (q : sheafSource J F B ⟶ sheafTarget J F B)
      (s : sheafTarget J F B ⟶ sheafSource J F B),
      s ≫ q = 𝟙 _ ∧ q ≫ s = a e ∧
      IsSheafTensorAction J F B a ∧
      IsSheafBalancedMap J F B q
